q: 1. The plain ends of cast iron pipes are joined by
explain: Dresser coupling is a mechanical joint used to connect plain-ended pipes, offering flexibility and ease of assembly.

q: 2. Garbage is a
explain: Garbage refers to decomposable solid/dry waste, specifically organic matter from kitchens and food handling.

q: 3. A pipe conveying sewage from the plumbing system of a single building to a common sewer is called
explain: House sewers (or house drains) connect the building's plumbing to the lateral or public sewer.

q: 4. A sewer which receives discharge of a number of houses sewers called a
explain: Lateral sewers collect waste from individual house sewers and discharge them into branch or main sewers.

q: 5. A combined system will be favourable when
options: the sewers are to be laid in rocks
the topography is flat necessitating deep excavation
the locality to be served had narrow streets
explain: Flat topography makes a combined system more favorable because laying two separate pipes would require twice the deep, expensive excavation.

q: 6. An egg-shaped cross-section of a sewer
options: is economical than circular cross section
is more stable than circular cross section
provides self cleaning velocity in dry weather
explain: The hydraulic radius of the egg shape at low flow levels ensures higher velocity compared to a circular pipe, maintaining self-cleaning conditions during dry weather.

q: 7. Manholes are, generally, located
options: at all junctions of main and branch sewers
explain: Manholes are essential maintenance access points required whenever the pipe path, slope, or size changes, and at junctions.

q: 8. The lower portion of a manhole is known as
explain: The working chamber is the lower section of the manhole where a person can stand to perform inspections or cleaning.

q: 9. Manholes on sewer lines are provided for
explain: The primary purpose of a manhole is to provide access for periodic cleaning and removal of blockages.

q: 10. A good trap should
options: provide an adequate water seal at all times
explain: The water seal is the most critical feature of a trap, preventing foul gases from entering the building while allowing waste water to flow.

q: 11. Ventilation of house drainage is required to
options: relive the pressure of foul gases
dilute the foul air in the drain
reduce the obnoxious effect of foul air
explain: Ventilation prevents air pressure buildup that could break water seals and helps keep the drainage system free of foul odors.

q: 12. In one pipe system of plumbing
options: the main pipe is connected directly to the drainage system
all the traps are fully ventilated
explain: In a one-pipe system, a single vertical pipe carries both soil (waste from toilets) and waste (from sinks/baths), requiring extensive ventilation for safety.

q: 13. A pipe used to carry discharge from sanitary fittings like bathrooms, kitchens etc. is called
explain: Waste pipes carry 'sullage'—water that does not contain human excreta.

q: 14. The percentage ratio of the oxygen available in sewage to the oxygen required to satisfy one stage of bio-chemical oxygen demand (B.O.D.) is termed as
explain: Relative stability indicates the ability of an effluent to resist putrefaction, expressed as the ratio of available oxygen to the total oxygen required for BOD.

q: 15. The secondary treatment of sewage is carried out by the use of
explain: Trickling filters (and activated sludge processes) are biological units used in secondary treatment to oxidize organic matter.

q: 16. The sewage is treated by aerobic bacteria action in
explain: Aerobic processes occur in trickling filters, oxidation ponds (upper layers), and even to a degree in secondary settling tanks if oxygen is present.

q: 17. The equipment used for cleaning the sewers easily is called
explain: Scrapers are pushed or pulled through sewers to remove accumulated silt and deposits from the pipe walls.

q: 18. A minimum amount of D.O. desirable in any water body is
explain: While 4 mg/L is a survival limit, 5 mg/L is generally considered the desirable minimum to support a healthy and diverse aquatic ecosystem.

q: 19. B.O.D. equation is
explain: The standard first-order reaction equation for BOD exerted at time t is $L_t = L(1 - 10^{-kt})$, where L is the ultimate BOD.

q: 20. Light is excluded in B.O.D. incubator to
explain: If light enters, algae will grow and produce oxygen via photosynthesis, which would give a false, lower BOD reading.

q: 21. For any waste ...........
options: C.O.D. may be less than B.O.D.
C.O.D. is always greater than B.O.D.
depending upon the percentage of biodegradable matter, it may be either way
explain: Chemical Oxygen Demand (COD) measures both biodegradable and non-biodegradable organic matter, whereas BOD only measures biodegradable matter. Therefore, COD is always greater than or equal to BOD.

q: 22. Presence of nitrogen in a waste water sample is due to the decomposition of ...........
explain: Proteins are complex organic compounds containing nitrogen. When proteins in sewage are decomposed by bacteria, they release nitrogen in various forms (ammonia, organic nitrogen).

q: 23. Combined system may be favoured where ............
options: rain fall is concentrated in a season of the year and D.W.F. is often fluctuating from day to day
rain fall is scattered throughout the year and D.W.F. is to small compared to storm water
rain fall is distributed throughout the year such that it is <= 10 * D.W.F.
city is on steep rocky slopes
explain: A combined sewer (carrying both sewage and storm water) works best when rainfall is frequent and predictable, keeping the sewers flushed.
Sullage refers specifically to domestic wastewater from kitchens and bathrooms that does not contain human excreta (night soil).

q: 25. Top space is left free in a sanitary sewer for ............
explain: Leaving space in the upper part of the pipe allows the system to accommodate sudden increases in flow volume without surging.

q: 26. Maximum flow in sewers may be taken as ............
explain: For design purposes, the peak or maximum flow is typically estimated as three times the average daily flow.

q: 27. Velocity of flow in a sewer should be between ............
explain: Sewers need a 'self-cleansing' velocity of at least 0.6 m/s to prevent settling, but must stay below 3 m/s to prevent erosion of the pipe material.

q: 28. Ovoid sewers are best suited for ............
options: combined system with very wide fluctuations
explain: Ovoid (egg-shaped) sewers maintain a better velocity during low-flow periods (dry weather) compared to circular pipes, making them ideal for systems with high variation.

q: 29. When fall in elevation is greater than 90 cm the manhole provided is called ............
explain: A drop manhole is used when a branch sewer enters a main sewer at a significantly higher elevation, preventing splashing and protecting the manhole structure from erosion.

q: 30. A syphon spillway is an arrangement to ............
options: divert excessive D.W.F. into open drain
divert excessive storm water into drain
divert excessive combine flow water into drain
explain: In combined systems, syphon spillways act as automatic relief valves to divert excess water (mixture of sewage and storm water) to a nearby watercourse during heavy rain.

q: 31. Sewage sickness is a sickness developed by ............
options: humans due to consumption of crops grown on sewage
plants because to harmful elements of sewage irrigation
land unable to accept any more loading of sewage
sewage itself due to pathogens within
explain: If too much sewage is applied to land without rest, the soil pores become clogged (anaerobic), preventing air from reaching roots and causing the land to become 'sick' and unproductive.

q: 32. An ideal crop of sewage irrigation is ............
explain: Crops like bananas are ideal because the edible part is high above the ground and protected by a skin, minimizing health risks compared to root vegetables or low-lying greens.

q: 33. Grit chamber had a detention period of ............
explain: Grit chambers are designed to remove heavy inorganic solids very quickly (usually in about 60 seconds) before they can reach and damage downstream pumps or treatment units.

q: 34. Velocity of flow through a grit chamber is ............
explain: The velocity is kept low enough (approx 0.3 m/s) to allow sand and grit to settle, but high enough to keep organic matter in suspension.

q: 35. Grit obtained in a grit chamber is used ............
explain: Because grit is largely composed of inorganic sand and gravel, it can be washed and reused in construction or as a fill material.

q: 36. Overflow rat of for primary clarifier is ............
explain: Primary clarifiers are typically designed with an overflow rate (surface loading) in the range of 20 to 30 cubic meters per square meter per day.

q: 37. Sedimentation aided by coagulation is rarely done for sanitary sewage because ............
options: time of treatment is further prolonged
sludge cannot be disposed of easily
chemicals may be harmful to living organisms of sewage
explain: Chemical coagulation produces a very large volume of sludge that is often difficult to dewater and digest compared to purely biological sludge.
